parameters.content:
# Set up your Concert System
1. Install the TypeSafe AI community node (@typesafe-ai/n8n-nodes-typesafe-ai; built with 0.9.0).
2. Create Header Auth: name X-Lesson-Key, value your own random secret. Select it on BOTH webhook nodes.
3. Select your OpenAI credential on Select lesson explanation and Retrieve dated sources. Select your TypeSafe AI credential on Identify concert question (Evaluate).
4. Publish this workflow; copy BOTH production webhook URLs.
5. Deploy the companion Node/Babylon website. Set N8N_WEBHOOK_URL, N8N_EVENTS_WEBHOOK_URL, N8N_WEBHOOK_SECRET and PUBLIC_ORIGIN on its server.

The existing public demo uses the creator’s backend. Importing this template does NOT connect your workflow to that website. Voice additionally needs server-side OpenAI and ElevenLabs credentials.

Source: https://github.com/Empower21/economics-of-everything-flow4gold
One workflow, two independent authenticated entry points; no sub-workflows.

Financial results use deterministic formulas. TypeSafe routes intent; OpenAI selects approved text. AI does not generate the financial figures. Simulation assumptions and listings are fictional.

## Validate lesson request

Receives the lesson webhook payload, performs initial validation and calculations, then decides whether the request can continue through the lesson flow.

## Explain input correction

Returns a webhook response explaining how the user should fix an invalid lesson request.

## Classify lesson intent

Uses a type-safe AI classification step and supporting code to identify the concert-economics question and determine whether the detected intent is supported with enough confidence.

## Assemble lesson response

For supported, confident intents, OpenAI selects 1–3 approved paragraph IDs and an allowed scene focus. Validation reconstructs authored text; invalid or unavailable model output uses a prepared explanation. Uncertain intent prompts clarification. It does not generate unchecked lesson text or financial numbers.

## Validate research request

Receives the event research webhook, validates the planning interval and request structure, then routes valid requests into sourcing or invalid requests to an error response branch.

## Return planning error

Sends a webhook response for invalid event research or planning requests.

## Prepare listing sources

Simulation returns clearly labeled fictional events for Atlanta, Berlin and Kingston. Live mode retrieves dated sources using OpenAI. Code checks city, dates and duplicates; external listings still require independent confirmation. The companion website server handles caching.

## Correlate research response

Records the research correlation details after either sourcing path and returns one consolidated research response to the webhook caller.
